definition: Solving a task with no examples at all — only an instruction — relying on knowledge already in the model.
details: Zero-shot means the model never saw a labeled example of the task, yet answers from its instruction and pre-trained knowledge. LLMs can reason zero-shot by being asked to think step by step, a simple technique that matches or beats earlier few-shot methods on many benchmarks.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. Think of it this way: Solving a task with no examples at all — only an instruction — relying on knowledge already in the model. And here is the clever part: Zero-shot means the model never saw a labeled example of the task, yet answers from its instruction and pre-trained knowledge. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Zero-Shot Learning — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.

citation.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS)
